summary: PASS — All core behaviors of the new editable 'NEEDS ESTIMATOR INPUT' UX verified live against a real Multi-Part RFQ (hot_rfq.msg, Jamestown Container / Sam's Club). The parse-asks block (data-testid 'parse-asks') now renders 10 flagged fields as FRIENDLY UI LABELS with section breadcrumbs (e.g. 'Pricing Mode' / Pricing Strategy, 'Print Mode' / Production Specs, 'Destination ZIP' / Freight, 'Colors — Back' / Production Specs, 'Board Grade' / Item Setup with component badge 'D/C Tray 1X (6 ct tray)', 'Inside Liner', 'Hand Gluing', etc.) — ZERO raw code variables shown (no 'bomItems[', '.state.', 'qtys (top-level)', or 'fscEnabled' strings leak into the user-facing text). Each editable row has data-testid 'parse-ask-{scope}-{key}' and an inline editor 'parse-ask-input-{scope}-{key}'. Editor controls match the field type: SELECT for Pricing Mode/Print Mode/Print Sides/Board Grade/Liners/Yes-No (Hand Gluing), INPUT[number] for Colors—Back, INPUT[text] for Destination ZIP. Editing Print Mode → 'Gloss' immediately rendered the '✓ set' green indicator on that row and changed the row border to green. Apply button label correctly read 'Apply Multi-Part (3 items)' (multi-part path). After clicking Apply, the modal closed, a toast 'Multi-Part applied — 3 components' appeared, and the main UI cost-summary panel now shows 'PRINT GLOSS' badge confirming the Print Mode edit landed in the quote (and that other parser values like Customer = Jamestown Container Corp., Project = Luva Bella Winery — Sam's Club Display, and 3 BOM components also applied). The async parser took ~45s on first run (12s on cache hit), well within the 2.5-min budget. The customer-search picker (AskCustomerPicker / 'parse-ask-input-job-custCode-results') could NOT be exercised because hot_rfq.msg yielded NO custCode ask (parser auto-detected the customer with high confidence). Code at FilesSec.jsx L913-960 implements the search/results path; behavior is verifiable but was not live-tested in this iteration.

test_results.customer_picker_search: NOT EXERCISED — hot_rfq.msg parsed with auto-detected customer and no custCode ask was raised. Code path AskCustomerPicker (FilesSec.jsx L913) is in place and wired to /api/customers search; not validated end-to-end this iteration. Recommend testing with a freshly created blank/unknown-customer RFQ to force the ask.

action_items: MINOR (testability): Item-scoped ask rows use data-testid='parse-ask-item-{key}' without itemIdx. When two different BOM components flag the SAME field (e.g. both items have an 'insideLiner' ask), the two rows share an identical data-testid (observed: 2× 'parse-ask-item-insideLiner' and 2× 'parse-ask-input-item-insideLiner' in the hot_rfq.msg run). Recommend changing FilesSec.jsx L721 + L735 to include itemIdx: `parse-ask-item-{itemIdx}-{key}` and `parse-ask-input-item-{itemIdx}-{key}`. Internal state (ekey) already keys edits by itemIdx, so this is purely a test-selector fix; user-facing behavior is correct because each row has its own React key and its own AskEditor instance.

OPTIONAL: Exercise the AskCustomerPicker path with an RFQ that does not have a recognized customer signature (or one where the model emits a custCode ask). All three sample RFQs in this run had high-confidence customer detection so the picker UI wasn't reachable from the live ask list.
critical_code_review_comments: parserFieldRegistry.js is clean — FIELD_META covers all the fields the parser actually emits; ALIAS map handles parser variant names (customerName/po/notes/fobMode/etc.); parseAskField regex correctly handles both 'bomItems[N].state.key' and 'bomItems[N].key' shapes plus the '(top-level)' suffix.
FilesSec.jsx normAsks (L419-423) gracefully falls through to a non-editable note row when meta lookup fails — good defensive coding so unmapped future fields don't crash the modal.

ekey() (L383) uses 'item:{idx}:{key}' — correct collision-free internal keying, even when two items flag the same field. The data-testid on the OUTER row doesn't carry itemIdx (see action item above), but this is a test-selector issue, not a functional one.

AskCustomerPicker (L913) properly debounces search calls via React state + setTimeout? — quick scan suggests it fires search on each keystroke past 2 chars; consider adding a 200ms debounce if rapid typing causes redundant /api/customers requests under load. Not blocking.

askCurrentValue (L401-415) correctly distinguishes bool fields (fscEnabled stored as boolean, surfaced as 'Yes'/'No'), array fields (qtys → comma-joined string), and item-scope fields stored under `it.state` vs the two BOM-level fields (`type`, `pcsPerSet`) stored at the item root. This matches the apply() merge path.
Modal correctly shows component name badge from `bomItems[itemIdx].desc` with fallback 'Item N+1' — matches what the user sees on the BOM tabs in the main view.

Reliable testids: parse-review-modal, parse-asks, parse-ask-{scope}-{key}, parse-ask-input-{scope}-{key}, parse-mp-banner, parse-mp-tab-{job|idx}, parse-review-apply. After Apply on a Multi-Part quote, verify the Print Mode by looking at the cost-summary right rail in the main UI which shows 'PRINT {SATIN|GLOSS|...}' badges per active BOM item.
